overall: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law on October 6 by failing to follow executive session procedures under Purpose 1 and by omitting topics from the October 6 and October 20 notices; it ordered compliance and minutes release.

allegations.summary: Board convened an October 6 executive session discussion of complaints without giving the subjects the 48-hour notice and other rights required under Purpose 1.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to follow certain procedural requirements for convening in executive session, including the failure to afford the individual certain rights under Purpose 1, on October 6

allegations.summary: The October 6 meeting notice did not list the distributed complaint reports as a discussion topic, though the Board discussed them in executive session.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, the Board should not have discussed the reports during this meeting.

allegations.summary: The October 20 meeting notice omitted the complaint discussion and written statement, which the Chair had pledged on October 6 to present at that meeting.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Board should not have discussed the complaints during its October 20 meeting because that discussion also was reasonably anticipated but the topic was not included in the meeting notice.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
Publicly release the portion of the October 6 executive session minutes related to the complaints, plus documents used in that discussion, subject to applicable exemptions and privilege.
Provide the subjects of the executive session with an unredacted version of the portion of the minutes concerning them.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law. In addition, we order the Board to publicly release the portion of its October 6 executive session minutes related to the complaints, as well as any documents used by the Board during that executive session discussion, subject to any applicable exemptions to the Public Records Law or the attorney-client privilege. Finally, we order the Board to provide the subjects of the executive session (Ms. Cesan and the Town employee) with an unredacted version of the portion of the minutes concerning them.
